opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll; full-time employees may have up to write, and admin is not permitted since Engineer does not own Payroll. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E045 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. With basic training, maximum access is read. Requested write, so grant read.
reason: The security record for E045 (Note 2) states the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). With basic training, the maximum access level is read. Douglas Salinas requested write to Payroll, which exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted. While the HR note claims full-time status, the security record identifies the employee as a contractor, and granting the more conservative level is appropriate given the conflicting employment records.
